items.title: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13) - Space
items.snippet: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13) Space
items.summary: A Space.com piece by Mike Wall, published 13 November 2026, says Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to lift off today from Starbase during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST, with SpaceX planning to catch both Super Heavy and Ship on the tower’s “chopstick” arms — something it has never done before. The plan is for Super Heavy to return about 6.5 minutes after launch, for Ship to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites (the second such batch after Flight 14 on 28 September) and then come back for a catch on 14 November about 22.5 hours after liftoff, or splash down in the Pacific if a catch is called off.

items.title: From SpaceX to Anthropic, markets have a new playbook for mega-share debuts - Reuters
items.snippet: From SpaceX to Anthropic, markets have a new playbook for mega-share debuts Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters analysis by Vidya Ranganathan, dated 12 Nov 2026, says Anthropic’s expected IPO next week is likely to follow SpaceX’s June debut, in which faster index inclusion by providers such as Nasdaq drew a large pool of passive buying in the first 15 days. It notes SpaceX shares were up 50% by day 3 from a $150 opening-day debut and stayed above the $135 IPO price for the first 15 days, before drifting lower ahead of lock-up expirations, and that Anthropic is similarly offering only about 6% of outstanding shares.

items.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get? - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get? Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A BeInCrypto article by Lockridge Okoth, dated 12 November 2026 and listed in Google News under Yahoo Finance, says Bloomberg reported that SpaceX–Tesla merger talks are progressing and a deal could be announced as early as December, though no terms are signed and the timetable could slip into 2027. It cites Bank of America analyst Alexander Perry saying SpaceX would buy Tesla with stock, leaving Tesla holders with about 47% of the combined company at a 20% premium on 20 October prices, and notes Tesla’s majority-of-outstanding-shares vote rule plus China regulatory risk could still block the deal.

items.title: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses — more than $24 billion at Starbase in Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona — expanding an AI business that already generated more than half of third-quarter revenue. The Arizona campus still needs county approval and faces a 2,400-signature petition ahead of a December public hearing, while a Starbase city notice describes a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility on about 444 acres, with the City Commission due to consider a property tax abatement on 9 December.

items.title: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress - Bloomberg.com
items.snippet: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress Bloomberg.com
items.summary: A Bloomberg report dated 12 November 2026, by Ryan Gould, Siddharth Philip and Dinesh Nair, citing people familiar with the matter, says SpaceX and Tesla are advancing merger talks and could announce a deal as early as December, though the companies have also considered slipping that announcement into early 2027. Boards and advisers are working through terms and the combined company’s governance; sources flagged isolating Tesla’s China operations from SpaceX’s U.S. government and defense work as a hurdle, and neither company immediately commented. Bloomberg.com itself was not directly reachable here; this summary is from the same Bloomberg article as carried by Bloomberg Línea.

items.title: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona - The New York Times
items.snippet: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona The New York Times
items.summary: A New York Times report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans a $74 billion investment to build data centers in Texas and Arizona. That tracks SpaceX’s own 12 November update, which puts more than $24 billion into a self-powered supercompute site at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and about $50 billion into a Cochise County, Arizona campus; the NYT page itself did not return a readable full text here, so this summary is from the headline plus that official company update.

items.title: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake - CNN
items.snippet: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake CNN
items.summary: A CNN report by Jackie Wattles, dated 12 November 2026, says SpaceX will try on Friday, in a window from 5:45 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. ET, to bring both stages of Starship back intact — the first attempt at full recovery of an orbital launch system, which the company has called the “holy grail” of rocketry. The piece notes that a Super Heavy V3 booster has not yet been caught, that catching the roughly 52-metre Ship from orbit in the tower arms has never been demonstrated, and that FAA rules require showing the chance of a casualty is below 1 in 1 million. CNN.com English did not return a usable page here; this is from CNN’s Spanish edition of the same Wattles article.

items.title: Zelensky says Musk-owned satellite system throttled again, Space X denies it - Axios
items.snippet: Zelensky says Musk-owned satellite system throttled again, Space X denies it Axios
items.summary: An Axios report by Barak Ravid and Thomas Novelly, dated 12 November 2026, says the Ukrainian government has asked the Pentagon and SpaceX to explain new restrictions it says are disrupting Starshield, the military version of Starlink used to operate reconnaissance and intercept drones — the second such complaint in recent weeks — and quotes SpaceX telling Axios: “This is false. There has been no change.” President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said units have recorded significant, systematic speed restrictions along the entire front line and in occupied areas, and a Ukrainian official told Axios the limits built over three days until 100% of missions failed, with Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires Denys Sienik saying the system shuts down when drones fly faster than 100 mph.

items.title: Why SpaceX Stock Popped After Nvidia's CEO News - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: Why SpaceX Stock Popped After Nvidia's CEO News The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Rich Smith, dated 12 Nov 2026, says SPCX was up about 2.9% Thursday morning while Nvidia was down about 4.6% after CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and attributes the pop to Musk replying that hiring Huang at SpaceX would be “an honor.” Smith argues that poaching Huang could help SpaceX’s chip and in-space AI data-center plans, but he says he does not know whether it will happen.

items.title: Building the future — Starbase and Cochise County supercompute investments
items.summary: SpaceX’s 12 November 2026 Updates post says it is advancing two supercompute projects — a facility at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and a campus in Cochise County, Arizona — that together represent more than $74 billion in planned U.S. investment. It plans more than $24 billion of new supercomputing at Starbase (on top of more than $15 billion already invested there), with the site generating its own power, plus $220 million to expand Brownsville’s water and wastewater capacity by 20 million gallons a day, and a roughly $50 billion Arizona campus expected to support about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs, using dry cooling with no planned industrial groundwater use.
items.timeSource: Official SpaceX posts linking the 12 November Updates item

items.title: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Keithen Drury, dated 12 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, argues that Super Intelligence — not Starlink or Starship — is the real reason SPCX could rally before 2027, noting SI revenue grew 830% year over year to $7.56 billion in Q3, more than half of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion total. He cites Musk’s view that annual recurring revenue could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, while warning that the stock could struggle if the market stays bearish on heavy AI spending.

items.title: Why SpaceX Stock Is Getting in the Way of a Tesla Merger - Barron's
items.snippet: Why SpaceX Stock Is Getting in the Way of a Tesla Merger Barron's
items.summary: A Barron’s column dated 12 November 2026 argues that SpaceX’s share-price slump is complicating a potential all-stock Tesla merger, because a lower SPCX price would mean issuing more shares to buy Tesla. Barron’s itself returned 401 here; as relayed by Yahoo Finance and Benzinga, its hypothetical math says a 15% premium deal would need about 2.3 SPCX shares per Tesla share at $200, versus about 3.2 shares at around $140, leaving Tesla holders with more than half the combined company versus about 43% at the higher price. Those figures are illustrative — neither company has agreed terms.

items.title: Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13 - Barchart.com
items.snippet: Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13 Barchart.com
items.summary: A Barchart column by Ebube Jones, published 12 Nov 2026, tells SPCX holders to mark Friday 13 Nov for Starship Flight 15, when SpaceX plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage with the launch tower’s mechanical arms — a first if it succeeds — after Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sept and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Jones notes shares have fallen almost 12% over the past month and that SpaceX and Tesla lost about $456 billion in combined market value after the midterms, argues a successful double catch could help the stock bounce back but would not erase valuation or spending concerns, and cites Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas at Overweight with a $300 price target plus a 40-analyst “Moderate Buy” consensus averaging $252.05.

items.title: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin - CNBC
items.snippet: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin CNBC
items.summary: A CNBC report dated 12 November 2026 says President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alleged fresh, systematic speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield service over Ukraine, with terminals disconnecting above 161 km/h (100 mph) and making it harder to intercept Russian jet-powered drones along the front line and in occupied territories. CNBC says it reached out to SpaceX and the White House for comment, notes similar limits were imposed in mid-October and lifted by 24 October, and places Zelenskyy’s remarks as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Prediction: This Will Be SpaceX's Stock Price in 5 Years - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: Prediction: This Will Be SpaceX's Stock Price in 5 Years The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Jennifer Saibil, dated 12 Nov 2026, notes that SPCX is down 11% from its first-day close and argues that if revenue compounds at 50% a year to $247 billion in trailing sales and the shares trade at 20 times sales, the stock could be worth $357 in five years, implying a $4.9 trillion market cap. She is hesitant to recommend it, citing uncertainty around AI competition and regulation and a still-rich 58 times sales multiple that she says will keep falling and thus limit how high the price can go.

items.snippet: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Today Will Be Worth This Much by 2029 Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Rick Orford, dated 12 November 2026 and carried by Yahoo Finance, sketches three earnings-based scenarios for what $1,000 in SPCX could be worth by 2029, citing Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, $4.4 billion of net income, 13.6 million Starlink subscribers and about $19.6 billion of capex. Its conservative case (30% annual sales growth, a 20 times price-to-sales multiple) implies about $810; the base case (45%, 25 times) about $1,400; and the optimistic case (60%, 30 times) about $2,260 — the author’s calculations, not a company forecast.

items.title: SpaceX launches 2nd mystery mission for US Space Force in 6-day span (video, photos) - Space
items.snippet: SpaceX launches 2nd mystery mission for US Space Force in 6-day span (video, photos) Space
items.summary: A Space.com report by Mike Wall, published 12 November 2026, says a Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg at 11:36 p.m. EST on 11 November (8:36 p.m. local) on the classified USSF-627 mission, SpaceX’s second such Space Force flight in six days after USSF-432 on 6 November. Both payloads are undisclosed — some experts have speculated they may be Starshield satellites for the Space Force’s Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio — and the USSF-627 booster (designation 1103, on its seventh flight) landed about 8.5 minutes after liftoff on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship; the flight was the 120th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the rocket’s 15th national-security mission of the year.

items.title: USSF-627 mission
items.summary: SpaceX’s official USSF-627 page now confirms that Falcon 9 lifted off at 8:36 p.m. PT on 11 November 2026 from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. It says this was the seventh flight for the first-stage booster, which had previously launched NROL-179, SDA-T1TL-E, SDA-T1TL-A and three Starlink missions, and that after stage separation the booster landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: SpaceX Shares Slip Amid Upcoming Starship Test Flight Jitters - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: SpaceX Shares Slip Amid Upcoming Starship Test Flight Jitters Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool market wrap by Robert Izquierdo, dated 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says SPCX closed at $139.75, down 2.33%, after early strength from the FCC accepting SpaceX’s application to acquire 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain Management faded as investors focused on Friday’s Starship Flight 15. He also flags the 8 December lock-up expiry and notes Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161%, including $7.6 billion from the AI business; volume was about 111 million shares, and the stock is down 13% since the 2026 IPO.

items.title: Nov. 13 Could Be a Huge Day for SpaceX Stock - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Nov. 13 Could Be a Huge Day for SpaceX Stock Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Johnny Rice, dated 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, treats Friday’s Starship Flight 15 as a major event for SPCX and quotes Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas calling a successful catch potentially “the biggest positive catalyst since the IPO.” SpaceX plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Starship upper stage at Starbase after a window opening around 5:45 p.m. ET, then fly more than 22 hours, complete about 14 orbits and deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before a Saturday catch attempt; the author notes that none of the latest V3 boosters have been caught yet and that a miss could push the payoff further out.

items.summary: The Motley Fool uses Street price targets to sketch what a $5,000 SPCX purchase might be worth by November 2027, citing a CNN-tracked median 12-month target of $245 (about 82% above the 6 Nov close of $134.27) and a low target of $118. It notes that 47 analysts cover the stock, with most rating it a buy, and stresses that targets are not guarantees.

items.title: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A TheStreet column by Hillary Remy and Dana Sullivan Kilroy, dated 10 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says Alphabet raised its SpaceX holding to about 555 million shares, up from 551.2 million, while paying SpaceX $920 million a month for xAI data-center capacity from October 2026 through June 2029 — a contract TheStreet puts at roughly $30 billion, covering about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs. The piece notes Alphabet booked an $8.7 billion third-quarter equity-securities loss driven mainly by the SpaceX share drop, that Google called the GPU arrangement bridge capacity for Gemini (either side can exit with 90 days’ notice after 2026), and that Google executive Don Harrison has resigned from SpaceX’s board.

items.title: Prediction: Here's How Much SpaceX Will Be Worth by the End of 2027 - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Prediction: Here's How Much SpaceX Will Be Worth by the End of 2027 Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Justin Pope, dated 10 November 2026 and carried on Yahoo Finance, predicts SPCX could finish 2027 around $250, about 65% above the then-current $134, after a $1.77 trillion IPO and a pullback to roughly the $135 offer price. The piece cites Q3 Super Intelligence revenue of $7.56 billion and Connectivity revenue of $5.25 billion with 13.6 million subscribers, and reaches that $250 target by annualizing the high end of Q1 2027 guidance to about $150 billion of 2027 revenue and applying a 20 times sales multiple, while warning of political and AI-industry risks.

items.title: SpaceX - Britannica
items.snippet: SpaceX Britannica
items.summary: The Google News link and the main Britannica page were blocked; Britannica’s Scholars encyclopedia entry by Alison Eldridge describes SpaceX as an American aerospace company founded by Elon Musk in 2002, now headquartered in Starbase, Texas, and covers Falcon, Dragon, Starlink and Starship plus the February 2026 xAI acquisition, a June 2026 IPO of 555.6 million shares at $135 that raised $75 billion and valued the company at about $1.77 trillion, and the August 2026 $60 billion purchase of Cursor. It says that as of June 2026 Starlink had more than 10,200 satellites in orbit and 12 million subscribers, and that after the xAI deal SpaceX made artificial intelligence one of its three main business segments alongside space and connectivity.

items.snippet: Elon Musk Just Gave the Top End of His SpaceX Revenue Forecast About a 2% Chance. His Best Guess Sits at the Bottom End. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: This Yahoo Finance story (also run by The Motley Fool) says Musk told the Baron Investment Conference that year-end 2027 annual recurring revenue is “quite likely” to top $500 billion — his “best guess,” not a promise — and put roughly 2% odds on $1 trillion. It notes even the low end would be five times a $100 billion December 2026 pace he discussed, while the stock was then only a little above the $135 IPO price and about 38% below a $225.64 52-week high.

An IR note the same day thanks Harrison, who had served since February 2015 and is President of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development at Google.

items.snippet: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms CNBC
items.summary: CNBC reports that Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Thursday after the midterms, taking combined market-cap losses since Tuesday’s close to more than $420 billion on concerns that Musk could face new probes and tighter regulation. The article says Musk was a major GOP donor (more than $470 million, per the Financial Times) even as most of the candidates he backed lost, and that his estimated wealth dropped to below $800 billion.

The guide recalls a first-day close a little above $160 and a brief spike above $225, followed by a bumpier trade often below the offer price; it is an explainer, not a recommendation.

items.title: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service - CNBC
items.snippet: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service CNBC
items.summary: CNBC says SpaceX struck a multiyear deal with Qualcomm to build base stations for Starlink Mobile, a planned U.S. cellular service meant to complement the satellite network, with a rollout targeted to begin next year. Financial terms were not disclosed; Qualcomm’s Durga Malladi called it a chance to advance 5G and eventually AI-native 6G, and CNBC notes Starlink already accounted for 36% of SpaceX revenue and 85% of operating profit in Q3.

items.snippet: Qualcomm signs major 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile network Reuters
items.summary: Reuters reported that Qualcomm signed a major 5G-infrastructure deal with SpaceX for the Starlink Mobile network; Reuters.com itself returned 401 here. Open coverage of the same announcement, including Qualcomm’s own release and CNBC, says Qualcomm will supply radio and baseband gear for a nationwide terrestrial 5G network that complements Starlink satellites, with deployment expected to start in 2027 and financial terms undisclosed.

items.title: 8-K — Item 8.01, Apollo GPU finance-lease commitment
items.summary: The 8-K says that on 24 Oct 2026 SpaceX signed a binding commitment for a master finance lease with an Apollo-managed lessor that will buy GPU pods and related equipment and lease them to SpaceX. The company expects about $40 billion of principal payments over roughly five-year tranche schedules, with closing targeted by year-end 2026 and deliveries in the first half of 2027; an IR release adds that the chips are next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs and that Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and KKR also committed.

The live EDGAR document could not be fetched here (403); contemporaneous descriptions of this filing put the registered reoffer amount at about 23.6 million Class A shares.

items.title: SpaceX reports third quarter 2026 results
items.summary: SpaceX’s official third-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion a year earlier, with net income of $4.4 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion. Super Intelligence revenue was $7.56 billion and Connectivity $5.25 billion, with 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers and $69 monthly ARPU; the company also completed its first revenue Starship mission, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.
items.timeSource: EDGAR acceptance of the Q3 2026 earnings 8-K (the press release is the 8-K exhibit)

items.title: 8-K — Q3 2026 earnings release
items.summary: This 8-K furnishes SpaceX’s official third-quarter 2026 earnings release as Exhibit 99.1 under Item 2.02. The exhibit is the same release summarised in the press item: revenue of $14.6 billion (up 161%), net income of $4.4 billion, and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion.

items.title: Acquisition of Cursor (Anysphere) — 8-K
items.summary: An 8-K says SpaceX closed its acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on 14 Aug 2026, converting outstanding Cursor stock into 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, plus 1,752,426 shares for vested RSUs before tax withholding. Unvested Cursor awards were assumed as about 29.1 million SpaceX RSUs and 44.4 million options, and the merger shares were issued in an unregistered Section 4(a)(2) transaction.
items.timeSource: EDGAR acceptance of the Cursor acquisition 8-K

items.title: 8-K — Cursor (Anysphere) acquisition
items.summary: This 8-K (Items 2.01 and 3.02) reports that SpaceX completed the Anysphere/Cursor merger on 14 Aug 2026 and issued unregistered Class A shares as merger consideration. Cursor stock converted into 389,289,254 SpaceX shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, with additional shares and assumed awards for Cursor RSUs and options.

items.title: SpaceX reports second quarter 2026 results
items.summary: SpaceX’s official second-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% from $4.1 billion, a net loss of $541 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 billion. The letter highlights two Starship V3 flight tests in 90 days, $14.1 billion of contracted cloud-services sales, the announced $60 billion Cursor deal, 12.0 million Starlink consumer subscribers at $66 ARPU, $47.5 billion of backlog, and $100 billion of cash and marketable securities after the IPO.

items.title: SpaceX closes IPO, including full exercise of underwriters’ option
items.summary: SpaceX’s IR release says the IPO closed on 15 Jun 2026 with 638,888,888 Class A shares issued, including the full underwriters’ option for 83,333,333 extra shares, for about $85.7 billion of gross proceeds. Class A shares had begun trading on 12 Jun 2026 on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under the ticker SPCX.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX prices IPO at $135.00 per share
items.summary: SpaceX priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135.00 and granted the underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 83,333,333 more shares at the same price. The IR release said trading was expected to start on 12 Jun 2026 on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas under SPCX, with closing slated for 15 Jun 2026.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX launches initial public offering roadshow
items.summary: SpaceX launched the IPO roadshow for 555,555,555 Class A shares, with an expected $135.00 offer price and the intended ticker SPCX on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas. The company also planned to grant underwriters a 30-day option for up to 83,333,333 additional shares.
